title: daily scratchpad - gpu ops & capacity reminders
content:
2026-03-04 - quick scratchpad (samira)

Top-of-day goals:
- triage alerts from last night (see INFRA-482) -> prioritize hotspots in eu-west-1
- finalize capacity bump plan for dedicated-gpu-pool-2 (target +20% for March 15 rollout)
- follow up with networking on MTU regression after kernel upgrade

TODO (today)
- [ ] Run GPU health sweep on dedicated-gpu-pool-1 (nvml, temp, ECC) - run before 11:00 PT
  - command: ./scripts/gpu-health-check.sh --pool dedicated-gpu-pool-1 --output /tmp/gpu-health-$(date +%F).log
- [ ] Validate autoscaler policy for batch workloads (policy: burst-to-4, min=2, max=16)
  - check: /infra/k8s/gpu-autoscaler/config.yaml (PR #234 touched scaling)
- [ ] Re-run perf benchmark for rlhf-inference v2 (seq-len=1024) to get updated latency numbers for pricing calc
- [ ] Confirm NVSwitch firmware on new p4d nodes (ticket #INFRA-490 placeholder)
- [ ] Post short update to #gpu-ops Slack (status + known work windows)

Notes / context:
- Last night's noises: 3x preemption spikes around 03:20 UTC in eu-west-1. Logs show long GC on node i-0a12cd34 -> infra suspect kernel+docker combo. Need to coordinate with SRE and CE.
- Capacity: finance gave provisional thumbs-up for +20% commit on dedicated capacity; we need firm cost model (per-token) before sales sign-off. Use recent batch perf numbers + cache hit ratio to estimate.
- Autoscaling: observed slow scale-up for cold-start batch jobs (30-45s). Potential fix: increase warm-pool size or enable quicker pre-warm hooks. Open question: trade-off cost vs latency for PLG customers.

Follow-ups / who to ping:
- @jorge (SRE): please check node i-0a12cd34 kernel + docker versions. Suspect 5.15. Last good known was 5.10.
- @karina (networks): confirm MTU change on subnet prod-eu-west-1-subnet-b after kernel upgrade (saw some fragmentation logs).
- @claire (finance): share updated cost estimate for +20% reserved GPUs by EOD Wed.

Quick commands / checks:
- k get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=i-0a12cd34
- sudo dmesg | grep -i -E "oom|gpu|nvlink|nvml"   (on suspect node)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 5

Temporary mitigation ideas:
- Add fallback routing for long-running requests to smaller model variant (keep client-side transparent): config route -> model_fallback: rlhf-inference-v2 -> rlhf-inference-v2-quantized
- Increase grace period for preemption to allow KV cache flushes (low-cost but reduces eviction churn)

Capacity planning bullets (for deck):
- Baseline: avg sustained tokens/day for dedicated customers = 1.2B (Feb)
- Peak P95 traffic spiky windows ~3x baseline, sustained 2-3h/day during EU morning hours
- Proposed commit: +20% dedicated GPUs (mix p4d:p3=60:40) -> expected throughput increase ~22% with current batching config
- Risks: driver/firmware mismatch, MTU/network fragmentation increasing latency for multi-node sharded models

Open questions / TODO backlog:
- Should we schedule rolling kernel downgrade on suspect nodes or instead pin docker runtime? (PROS/CONS in notes)
- Add automated NVSwitch firmware check to node-provisioning pipeline
- Document warm-pool sizing heuristics for batch workloads in Confluence page (link above)

Meeting notes (sync with SRE 2026-03-04 14:00 PT):
- agenda: incident follow-up (03:20 UTC), capacity commit prep, autoscaler tuning
- outcome: SRE will isolate 2 nodes for deeper debug, infra will draft capacity cost sheet, networks to double-check MTU config

Misc quick reminders:
- rotate k8s service account keys for gpu-autoscaler next week
- backup /etc/docker/daemon.json before testing any change
- run a small canary for the kernel change on staging (2 nodes) and measure GC latency for 24h

Notes-to-self:
- keep notes terse here; move final summaries to confluence page once nailed down
- remember to tag related PRs and Jira tickets with "gpu-ops" for traceability

---
History: copies of previous scratchpads in users/ (daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-0*) . This is the working file for March incident/capacity work.
